newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bond yields end off-peak after thin session.
newsitem.headline: NZ bond yields end off-peak after thin session.

text.p: New Zealand debt markets ended bid on Friday, thanks in part to strength in the Trade-Weighted Index, but trade was thin across the curve.
Strength in the Trade-Weighted Index, spurred by talk of renewed Samurai issues, was supportive for the short end.
In the bonds, there was some short covering towards the end, buying from offshore in the long bonds and a general lack of selling.
"We just got a bit cheap -- cheap to Australia, cheap to the U.S. and cheap nominally," said one Auckland bond dealer.
"When the buying came in there was very little selling to meet that," he said.
There was some Samurai-related interest in the short end of the curve as well.

Looking ahead, tonight's U.S. non-farm payrolls data, Wednesday's New Zealand futures closeout, Thursday's economic and fiscal update and Friday's Reserve Bank forecasts were expected to set direction for the medium term.
